idiom_name: Foundation temporary file (or shared container) plus UUID name as the claim check
implementation_notes: Foundation has no messaging seam, so the structure is hand-written: write the payload into a store location - FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory with a UUID-based name for a local store, an app-group or shared container when several processes or targets must reach it - send only the file name or URL, and read it back lazily with FileHandle when the consumer needs it. Inside one process the store buys nothing, because Data is copy-on-write and passing a Data value is already passing a reference until somebody mutates it; the file/token form earns its keep once the payload must survive process boundaries, memory limits or a background execution window. Keep an expiry or deletion rule and put long-lived payloads in Application Support rather than tmp, because temporary directories are purged unpredictably and are excluded from backup.
code_sketch:
let url = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
    .appendingPathComponent(UUID().uuidString).appendingPathExtension("payload")
try payload.write(to: url, options: .atomic)          // payload goes to the store
await channel.send(.init(orderId: id, claimCheck: url.lastPathComponent))
// consumer: let handle = try FileHandle(forReadingFrom: storeDir.appendingPathComponent(msg.claimCheck))
pitfalls: Temporary directories are reaped by the OS and excluded from backup, so a token that is valid at send time can dangle at redemption time; long-lived claims belong in Application Support with a deliberate backup policy.
FileHandle and the modern file APIs must be closed explicitly (and open files may not be removable on all platforms), so an abandoned handle leaks descriptors and blocks cleanup.

Cross-process sharing needs a shared container plus coordination: a URL inside one app's sandbox is not readable by another process, and iCloud/ubiquity URLs add asynchronous materialisation before the file can be read.
